description: Agent-based social diffusion model for household adoption of a city recycling program under peer influence, policy incentives, and media outreach on a dynamic social network.

modules.name: NetworkDynamics
modules.description: Builds the initial social network with homophily and updates edges via rewiring.

notes: Centrality can be degree-normalized to [0,1] by dividing by max degree.
Ensure network remains connected with a minimal degree > 0; if node becomes isolated, attach to nearest neighbor by attitude.

modules.name: SocialInfluence
modules.description: Computes perceived peer adoption via exponential moving average and transforms it into a social signal.

update_rule.pseudocode:
for each person i:
  neighbors <- N(i)
  if neighbors not empty:
    if neighbor_weighting == 'uniform':
      peer_adopt <- mean(adoption_state[j] for j in neighbors)
    else:
      weights <- degree[j]/sum(degree[k] for k in neighbors)
      peer_adopt <- sum(weights[j]*adoption_state[j] for j in neighbors)
  else:
    peer_adopt <- global_adoption_rate_previous_day
  # Exponential moving average memory
  p_old <- perceived_peer_adoption[i]
  p_new <- memory_decay * p_old + (1 - memory_decay) * peer_adopt
  perceived_peer_adoption[i] <- clamp(p_new, 0, 1)
  # Nonlinear norm sensitivity
  noise <- Normal(0, attention_noise_std)
  social_signal[i] <- tanh(local_norm_sensitivity * (perceived_peer_adoption[i] - 0.5)) + noise
  social_signal[i] <- clamp(social_signal[i], -1, 1)
notes: Global adoption rate from AggregationAndReporting t-1; use 0 if t=0.
tanh transform captures norm internalization; adjustable by local_norm_sensitivity.

modules.name: PolicyAndMedia
modules.description: Generates time-varying incentives and media outreach intensity by neighborhood with budget constraints and feedback to adoption progress.

update_rule.pseudocode:
for each neighborhood n:
  if policy_start_day <= t <= policy_end_day and Neighborhood[n].incentive_budget_remaining > 0:
    # Feedback rule: stronger incentives if behind target
    gap <- max(0, target_adoption_goal - Neighborhood[n].adoption_rate)
    incentive <- policy_multiplier_global * (incentive_per_signup_base * (1 + gap))
    incentive <- min(incentive, Neighborhood[n].incentive_budget_remaining)
  else:
    incentive <- 0
  signal.incentive_per_signup_by_neighborhood[n] <- incentive
  # Media schedule: base + pulse
  phase <- (2*pi*t)/media_pulse_period_days
  media_intensity <- media_intensity_base + media_pulse_amplitude * max(0, sin(phase))
  # Modulate by neighborhood performance (more media if lagging)
  media_intensity <- media_intensity * (1 + 0.5*gap)
  signal.media_intensity_by_neighborhood[n] <- media_intensity
  # Reach probability modifier maps intensity to reach uplift
  signal.media_reach_prob_modifier_by_neighborhood[n] <- min(0.5, media_intensity * 0.2)

# Budget update happens in Aggregation step when new adopters are counted and incentive payouts are deducted.
notes: policy_multiplier_global is implied by Neighborhood.policy_multiplier at init; operationally multiply incentive by neighborhood-specific multiplier.
Budget is decremented by new_adopters * incentive_per_signup after AdoptionDecision.

modules.name: AdoptionDecision
modules.description: Computes adoption probabilities and transitions non-adopters to adopters using a logistic utility with stochasticity and capacity capping.

update_rule.pseudocode:
candidates <- [i | i not adopted]
# Compute raw probabilities
for i in candidates:
  n <- neighborhood_id[i]
  inc_effect <- incentive_sensitivity[i] * signal.incentive_per_signup_by_neighborhood[n]
  media_reach <- media_reach_prob[i] + signal.media_reach_prob_modifier_by_neighborhood[n]
  media_effect <- media_reach * signal.media_intensity_by_neighborhood[n]
  cost_term <- base_cost * cost_income_scaling * (1 / max(1, income[i])) * cost_sensitivity[i]
  util <- beta0 + beta_peer * social_signal[i] + beta_attitude * (attitude_env[i]-0.5) + beta_incentive * inc_effect + beta_media * media_effect - beta_cost * cost_term + centrality_weight * centrality[i]
  p[i] <- 1 / (1 + exp(-util/decision_temperature))
# Optional capacity cap to avoid unrealistic surges
cap <- max_daily_adoption_fraction * len(candidates)
sum_p <- sum(p[i] for i in candidates)
scale <- 1.0 if sum_p <= cap or cap <= 0 else (cap / sum_p)
for i in candidates:
  if rand() < p[i] * scale:
    adoption_state[i] <- 1
    adoption_time[i] <- t
notes: decision_temperature > 0 smooths the logistic; smaller values increase determinism.

modules.name: DisadoptionChurn
modules.description: Allows adopters to churn (dis-adopt) based on dissatisfaction and costs; updates satisfaction state.

update_rule.pseudocode:
for each person i with adoption_state == 1:
  # Update satisfaction: increases with habit formation, decreases with implicit costs
  sat_old <- satisfaction[i]
  habit_gain <- satisfaction_update_rate * 0.02
  cost_penalty <- satisfaction_update_rate * churn_sensitivity_cost * cost_sensitivity[i] * 0.01
  sat_new <- sat_old + habit_gain - cost_penalty
  sat_new <- (1 - dissatisfaction_memory_decay) * sat_new + dissatisfaction_memory_decay * sat_old
  satisfaction[i] <- clamp(sat_new, 0, 1)
  # Churn probability if satisfaction falls below threshold
  if satisfaction[i] < satisfaction_threshold:
    p_churn <- churn_rate_base + churn_sensitivity_cost * (satisfaction_threshold - satisfaction[i])
    if rand() < clamp(p_churn, 0, 1):
      adoption_state[i] <- 0
notes: Disadoption re-opens the possibility to adopt later.
Set churn_rate_base low to keep churn rare unless satisfaction is low.

modules.name: AggregationAndReporting
modules.description: Aggregates daily adoption metrics, updates neighborhood budgets, and exposes observables.

update_rule.pseudocode:
# Compute global metrics
N <- population_size
adopters_today <- count(i where adoption_time[i] == t)
disadopters_today <- count(i where adoption_state changed 1->0 at t)
current_adopters <- count(i where adoption_state[i] == 1)
adoption_rate <- current_adopters / N
new_adopters_daily <- max(0, adopters_today)
cumulative_adopters <- cumulative_adopters_prev + new_adopters_daily - disadopters_today
# By-neighborhood metrics and budget updates
for each neighborhood n:
  ids <- persons in n
  rate_n <- mean(adoption_state[i] for i in ids)
  observable.adoption_rate_by_neighborhood[n] <- rate_n
  Neighborhood[n].adoption_rate <- rate_n
  payouts <- signal.incentive_per_signup_by_neighborhood[n] * count(i in ids where adoption_time[i] == t)
  Neighborhood[n].incentive_budget_remaining <- max(0, Neighborhood[n].incentive_budget_remaining - payouts)
# Expose smoothed observables if smoothing_window_days>1
observable.adoption_rate_daily <- Smooth(adoption_rate, window=smoothing_window_days)
observable.new_adopters_daily <- Smooth(new_adopters_daily, window=smoothing_window_days)
observable.cumulative_adopters_daily <- cumulative_adopters
cache global_adoption_rate_previous_day <- adoption_rate
notes: Smoothing uses simple moving average with centered or trailing window; trailing recommended.
Cumulative adopters accounts for disadoptions by subtracting disadopters.

initialization.assignments: Persons are assigned to neighborhoods uniformly at random; attributes drawn from specified distributions; network built per NetworkDynamics rules.

algorithms.network_generation: Watts–Strogatz small-world or Barabási–Albert scale-free using networkx.
algorithms.homophily_rewiring: Edge swap procedure to increase assortativity on attitude.
algorithms.social_signal_ema: Exponential moving average with memory_decay; tanh nonlinearity.
algorithms.adoption_choice: Logistic choice with temperature; optional aggregate cap on expected adoptions.
algorithms.churn_process: Thresholded stochastic churn with satisfaction dynamics.
algorithms.smoothing: Trailing moving average over smoothing_window_days for observables.
